messages:
rachel: Quick question — for the Console UI rollout I want clarity: should the automatic recovery/fallback policy show a small set of recommended presets or expose all triggers (latency, 5xx, token_quota) as toggles?
kevin: leaning presets. most users confuse too many toggles. presets + an "advanced" panel? :thumbsup:
devin: presets + advanced seems reasonable. but we need to ensure telemetry names are consistent so metrics/alerts remain meaningful when people pick presets. i.e. do not create opaque aggregated events that hide the actual trigger.
marco: UX note — if we show presets, name them by outcome not mechanism. e.g. "serve-degraded-model", "serve-from-cache", "fail-fast". less technical for product teams.
rachel: good call. proposal: default preset = "route-to-small-model + cache"; conservative = "fail-fast with alert"; aggressive = "route-to-smaller-model only".
kevin: what counts as "route-to-small-model" in the config? we need deterministic matching for audit logs. we should include the model family + quantization tag.
marco: agree. audit log entries should include the full policy snapshot that was active when the fallback fired. otherwise SRE can't repro.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: feature-flag rollouts/auto-recover v0.3 started in staging :rocket:
kevin: also API debate: current internal API has route_policy object that mixes routing and fallback. i'd prefer splitting into route_policy and recovery_policy so RBAC and quotas can be evaluated separately.
device: (typo) devin: +1 to split. quotas are orthogonal — you may want fallback without honoring the same per-route token quota.
rachel: hmm, splitting surfaces another UX problem — if two separate objects exist, Console needs to show inherited behavior and merged view. Can we show a single preview that computes final effective policy?
kevin: yes, preview required. preview should show: current policy -> trigger conditions -> action -> expected token cost delta (estimate). telemetry team can feed cost model.
marco: can we embed a short eval that simulates 50 requests and shows expected latency/cost diff? helpful for customers.
de vin: devin: simulation is great but expensive. maybe a dry-run mode that samples real traffic and reports back after 24h.
rachel: let's not block shipping on simulation. MVP: presets + advanced, split APIs, preview with estimated cost delta, audit log includes policy snapshot and trigger reason.
kevin: naming/time semantics for triggers: should we use "error_rate > 5% over 1m" or "consecutive 5xx >= 3"? both are useful. I'd add both as trigger types: rolling-window and consecutive-count.
marco: UI should default to rolling-window for novices and expose consecutive-count in advanced.
rachel: sample policy (for the engineers):
```
recovery_policy:
  id: "rp_auto_smallroute_01"
  preset: "route-to-small-model+cache"
  triggers:
    - type: "rolling_error_rate"
      window: "1m"
      threshold_pct: 5
    - type: "consecutive_errors"
      count: 3
  actions:
    - type: "route"
      target_model: "gptx-small@q4_8bit"
    - type: "kv_cache"
      ttl_seconds: 60
  audit: true
```
kevin: that looks good. small suggestion: include a telemetry_tag field so metrics pipeline can map events to the preset (e.g., telemetry_tag: "preset_smallroute_v1").
de vin: devin: please also include a human_readable_reason in the audit log entry that explains why the trigger fired (e.g., "rolling_error_rate 6.3% over 1m"). makes postmortems easier.
rachel: agreed. Also retention: audit logs must be queryable for 90d by default (enterprise opts). add link to retention policy in Console.
kevin: one last thing: fallback should be opt-in for routes that serve regulated content — we must show a clear checkbox "allow automatic recovery actions for this route" and default off for private deployments.
marco: +1. add a separate approval flow for dedicated/private customers — can require audit config + notification to security group.
ops-bot: infra-bot: FYI we've added two new telemetry events: recovery.policy_applied and recovery.policy_evaluated. schema in #eng-infra.
rachel: thanks. next steps: kevin/devin to draft API spec for recovery_policy split + telemetry tags; marco to mock console presets + preview; i'll consolidate and post a short doc for PM review by EOD Friday.
kevin: I can have the API draft in PR by tomorrow morning.
de vin: i'll add the analytics schema as a follow-up.
marco: mockups later today.
rachel: awesome — thanks team. :tada:
